cards.text: Elisha, a prophet of the LORD, heads back to Gilgal. The sons of the prophets are sitting at his feet. But times are hard in the land right now.

cards.question: While Elisha is back in Gilgal, there's a ___ in the land.

cards.text: Food's running short, and Elisha tells his attendant to put on the large pot and boil some stew. Not the medium pot, friend, the LARGE one.

cards.question: Elisha's attendant is boiling up a large pot of stew. Who is it for?

cards.text: One of them goes out to the field to gather herbs, finds a wild vine, and loads up on wild gourds, as many as his garment can hold. That's not a garment anymore, friend, that's a SHOPPING CART.

cards.question: When the man cuts the wild gourds into the pot of stew, everybody knows what they are.

cards.text: They pour the stew out for the men, and the second they taste it, I bet every face in the room changes. I know that face, friend: it's the face a baker makes when the sugar jar turns out to be the SALT jar.

cards.question: What do the men cry out to Elisha after they taste the stew?

answers.text: There is death in the pot
The stew is far too bitter

cards.question: After crying out about the stew, the men keep eating it anyway.
Elisha doesn't dump the pot of stew. Instead he calls for some ___.

cards.text: Elisha throws the flour into the pot and says to pour it out for the people to eat. Flour. Into STEW. Friend, I've put flour into a LOT of things, and stew was never once on the list.

cards.question: After Elisha throws the flour into the stew, there's nothing harmful left in the pot.

cards.text: Then a man from Baal-shalishah comes to the man of God with a sack of twenty loaves of barley bread from the first ripe grain. TWENTY, friend, that's like somebody walking into the office with twenty cookie boxes and becoming the hero of the whole building.

cards.question: Elisha says to give the twenty loaves of barley bread to the ___ to ___.
Elisha's servant questions the plan for the twenty loaves. What's his problem?

answers.text: There are a hundred men to feed
The bread was meant for the priests
The loaves are too hard to eat

cards.text: Twenty loaves, a hundred men, and my math says that's a CRUMB apiece. But Elisha says that line again, "Give it to the people to eat," and then he tells his servant what the LORD says.

cards.question: According to what the LORD says, what will happen when the hundred men eat the twenty loaves?

answers.text: They will eat and have some left over
Each man will get only a small piece
The bread will last until the famine ends

cards.text: So the servant sets the twenty loaves in front of the hundred men. Moment of truth, friend.

cards.question: The bread runs out before all hundred men get to eat.

cards.text: They eat, and there's bread LEFT OVER, "according to the word of the LORD." Friend, I have never once had a batch come out of the oven BIGGER than the dough I put in.

findings.problem: This story card runs four sentences: the Elisha sentence, then "Flour.", "Into STEW." and the "Friend, I've put flour..." line. Fragments still count as sentences. Trim the joke so the card is no more than 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Someone has spoiled the pot" is close in meaning to the right answer "There is death in the pot." One of the men did ruin the stew with the gourds in 2 Kings 4:39, so a baker could argue it's right. Replace it with an answer that clearly isn't what the men cried out.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The sons of the prophets appear here for the first time, but the card never says who they are. Add a simple identification, such as a group of prophets gathered around Elisha.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
